image.proof_notes: Commons file shows O'Donoghue's named black-and-white fascia (15 O'DONOGHUE'S 15) and storefront on Merrion Row, Dublin. PROPERTY SWAP: Kehoe's (Dublin) had no usable Commons named facade/interior — swapped to O'Donoghue's Merrion Row (shortlist swap pool).

facts.one_liner: Dublin Merrion Row music pub—black-and-white 15 O'DONOGHUE'S 15 fascia and window lanterns.
facts.why_go: O'Donoghue's at 15 Merrion Row is a Dublin traditional-music landmark: an 18th-century grocery/shebeen that became a full pub, made famous after Paddy and Maureen O'Donoghue took over in 1934 and nurtured nightly sessions; The Dubliners helped cement its folk-revival fame in the 1960s. The photo matches the glossy black-and-white storefront: white "15 O'DONOGHUE'S 15" fascia, multi-pane display window packed with copper lanterns and wheat sheaves, Guinness "for sure!" sign, and the tiled "HYNES" threshold recalling a later proprietor. Live Irish music still runs seven nights a week; Oliver Barden's family continues the house tradition with guests and rooms upstairs.
facts.best_time: Weekday late afternoon for a seat and façade photo before the evening session; Friday from 6:30pm and Saturday from 5:30pm fill earliest. Sunday all-day music suits a longer visit—arrive early for a bar stool.
facts.how_to_get_there: 15 Merrion Row, Dublin 2, between St Stephen's Green and Merrion Square. LUAS Green Line stops at St Stephen's Green and Dawson Street (~5 minutes' walk); Dublin Bus routes 15b, 19, 39A, 38, 70 and S2 serve the area; Pearse DART is about 800 m.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official odonoghues.ie; drinks list Jan 2026: bar open daily from 10:30am; live trad Mon–Thu 8pm–midnight, Fri from 6:30pm, Sat from 5:30pm, Sunday all day). Not Kehoe's on South Anne Street—this is the Merrion Row house. Busy music nights stand-room only.

facts.one_liner: Lisbon Chiado cervejaria—dual CERVEJARIA Da TRINDADE awnings on Rua Nova da Trindade 20C/20D.
facts.why_go: Cervejaria Trindade bills itself as Portugal's oldest and most beautiful brewery-restaurant: a former convent site that survived earthquake and fires, now cervejaria, marisqueira, petiscaria, bar and museum with celebrated azulejo panels. The photo matches the light-stone dual entrance: matching tan awnings lettered "CERVEJARIA Da TRINDADE" with blue "T" shields, carved lintels "20D" and "20C," central menu board, and calçada portuguesa underfoot with tram tracks in frame. Visit Lisboa lists it for Portuguese steaks, seafood and beer between Chiado and Bairro Alto; tourist visits of the historic rooms run outside meal peaks.
facts.best_time: Weekday lunch or mid-afternoon for clearer exterior photos and easier seating; Friday–Saturday evenings run later (to 1am). Book or arrive early for dinner in the tiled halls.
facts.how_to_get_there: Rua Nova da Trindade 20C, 1200-303 Lisboa, between Chiado and Bairro Alto. Metro Baixa-Chiado (Blue/Green) is a short walk; several trams and city buses serve Chiado / Rua da Misericórdia edges.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official cervejariatrindade.pt: Sun–Thu 12:00–00:00, Fri–Sat and holiday eves 12:00–01:00; tourist visits ~10:00–12:00 and 15:00–19:00). Recognized Lisbon cultural heritage / Loja com História—busy tourist cervejaria; reserve for peak dinner.

image.attribution: Photo: Gerd Eichmann, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts.one_liner: Vienna Fleischmarkt/Griechengasse inn—Griechenbeisl iron sign, Habsburg eagle, alley terrace.
facts.why_go: Griechenbeisl at Griechengasse 9 / Fleischmarkt 11 claims to be Vienna's oldest inn, serving guests for centuries under names such as Gasthaus zum gelben Adler before Greek traders gave the lane its "Griechen" identity. The photo looks down the cobbled alley: peach façade with "HAUS MIT GOTISCHEM WOHNTURM / Griechengasse 9" plaque, Austrian flags, hanging double-headed eagle and ornate "Griechenbeisl" iron sign, checkered terrace cloths and waiters under white umbrellas. Inside, historic rooms including the Mark Twain Room still serve Wiener Schnitzel, Tafelspitz and Kaiserschmarrn; vienna.info lists daily dining.
facts.best_time: Weekday mid-afternoon for a quieter alley photo and terrace seat; Friday–Sunday open from midday and fill for dinner. Reserve online or by phone—last orders around 22:00.
facts.how_to_get_there: Griechengasse 9 / Fleischmarkt 11, 1010 Vienna, in the Innere Stadt near Schwedenplatz. U1/U4 Schwedenplatz or tram lines along the Ring / Franz-Josefs-Kai; short walk into the Greek Quarter lanes.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official griechenbeisl.at: typically Mo–Thu 14:00–23:00, Fr–Su 12:00–23:00, with seasonal daily 12:00–23:00 from mid-August; last order 22:00; vienna.info lists daily 12:00–23:00). Historic tourist Beisl—book ahead for peak evenings. Distinct from other Vienna beerhalls.

image.attribution: Photo: C.Stadler/Bwag, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts.one_liner: Salzburg Mülln monastery brewery—mustard-yellow Augustiner Bräustübl Mülln arches and church dome.
facts.why_go: Augustiner Bräu Kloster Mülln has brewed in Salzburg's Mülln district at the foot of the Mönchsberg since Augustinian hermits founded the brewery in 1621—Austria's largest beer inn today, not Munich's Augustiner-Keller. The photo shows the mustard-yellow Bräustübl: blue Gothic "Augustiner Bräustübl Mülln" lettering over a four-arch loggia, hanging iron brewery sign, green-domed parish church tower behind, and a red-ended wooden tun in the car park. Inside, Märzen pours from wooden barrels into steins across halls and a 1,400-seat beer garden; Schmankerlgang stalls serve regional snacks—cash only.
facts.best_time: Weekday from 15:00 opening for space in the halls; weekends and holidays from 14:30 and fill fast in summer garden season. Closed 24/25/31 Dec and 1 Jan—check augustinerbier.at before holidays.
facts.how_to_get_there: Lindhofstraße 7, Salzburg (Mülln), northwest of the Altstadt. Buses 4, 7, 9, 20, 21, 24, 27, 28 to Landeskrankenhaus; S-Bahn stop Mülln-Altstadt a few minutes' walk; large free car park in front of the yellow façade.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official augustinerbier.at: Bräustübl Mon–Fri 15:00–23:00, Sat–Sun & holidays 14:30–23:00; closed 24/25/31 Dec & 1 Jan). Cash only—no cards. This is Salzburg Mülln monastery brewery, never Munich Augustiner-Keller.

image.proof_notes: Commons file shows Els Quatre Gats / 4 Gats named Modernista arched entrance into the café-tavern, Barcelona.

facts.one_liner: Barcelona Gothic Quarter Modernista café—brick arch, iron lantern, and lit 4 CATS entrance.
facts.why_go: Els Quatre Gats (4 Gats) opened 12 June 1897 on the ground floor of Josep Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Martí, inspired by Paris's Le Chat Noir and backed by Pere Romeu with painters Santiago Rusiñol, Ramon Casas and Miquel Utrillo. The night photo matches the Neo-Gothic brick pointed arch: ornate hanging lantern, stained-glass transom circles, gold "4 CATS" menu frame, checkered floor and blue-white tiled wainscot visible through the open door. Young Picasso showed early work here and designed the menu lettering; today it remains a Catalan restaurant in the Barri Gòtic.
facts.best_time: Tuesday–Saturday from late morning for lunch and a clearer arch photo; Sundays close mid-afternoon (12:00–17:00). Mondays closed—plan around that weekly rest day.
facts.how_to_get_there: Carrer de Montsió 3, 08002 Barcelona, in the Barri Gòtic near Portal de l'Àngel / Plaça de Catalunya. Metro Catalunya or Urquinaona; short walk from the cathedral and Gothic Quarter lanes.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official 4gats.com: Tue–Sat 11:00–24:00, Sun 12:00–17:00, closed Mondays). Historic Modernista restaurant—reserve for dinner; tourist landmark inside Casa Martí.

facts.one_liner: Asakusa corner bar since 1880—KAMIYA BAR / 神谷バー brick façade and green-tiled awning.
facts.why_go: Kamiya Bar at 1-1-1 Asakusa claims Japan's first Western-style bar, founded by Denbei Kamiya in 1880 and housed since 1921 in the present brick Kamiya Building (Registered Tangible Cultural Property). The photo shows the Asakusa corner: red "KAMIYA BAR" letters atop the grey upper bay, vertical yellow 神谷バー sign, white Japanese fascia over a distinctive green-tiled sidewalk awning, and Route 6 / Edo-dōri street signs. Order the house Denki Bran (created 1882)—tickets purchased at the entrance for the 1F bar; a shop on Kaminarimon Street sells bottles to take away.
facts.best_time: Weekday opening from 11:00 for space before the evening rush; last order 19:30. Closed Tuesdays and two Mondays each month—check the official calendar before you go.
facts.how_to_get_there: 1-1-1 Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo 111-0032, on the corner facing Kaminarimon / Asakusa Station. 1–2 minutes from Tokyo Metro Ginza Line Exit 3, Toei Asakusa Line Exit A5, or Tobu Skytree Line main exit.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official kamiya-bar.com: 11:00–20:00, last order 19:30; closed Tuesdays and two Mondays monthly; 1F bar is ticket-entry, cash-leaning—cards accepted upstairs/shop rules as posted). Denki Bran is the signature; not a hotel bar elsewhere in Tokyo.

facts.one_liner: Sydney Millers Point sandstone corner—HERO OF WATERLOO lettering, 1843 date, hanging portrait sign.
facts.why_go: The Hero of Waterloo at 81 Lower Fort Street is a convict-built sandstone hotel established 1843 in Millers Point / The Rocks—heritage-listed and still trading as pub, restaurant and live-music house. The photo matches the sharp corner: dark "HERO OF WATERLOO" block letters between floors, hanging Wellington portrait sign, vertical "1843 / SYDNEY" and "81 LOWER FORT STREET" inscriptions, and outdoor tables under trees on the slope. Cellar tours and ghost lore sit alongside James Squire taps and weekend bands—classic Rocks sandstone atmosphere.
facts.best_time: Weekday lunch or mid-afternoon for a clearer corner photo and quieter bar; weekend evenings bring live music crowds. Hours can shift for events—confirm on heroofwaterloo.com.au/contact.
facts.how_to_get_there: 81 Lower Fort Street, Millers Point NSW 2000 (The Rocks), corner of Lower Fort Street. Walk from Circular Quay / The Rocks, or bus routes along Argyle / George Street edges; Light Rail to The Rocks / Barangaroo then uphill.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official heroofwaterloo.com.au active; contact lists current daily hours—confirm by phone (02) 9252 4553 as special-event hours vary). Heritage sandstone landmark—cellar tours by arrangement; busy weekend music nights.

ad.destination_query: The Hero of Waterloo, Sydney, Australia

facts.one_liner: Buenos Aires San Telmo corner café—BAR EL FEDERAL oval sign at Carlos Calvo & Perú.
facts.why_go: Bar El Federal occupies a nineteenth-century corner at Carlos Calvo 599 / Perú in San Telmo, listed among Buenos Aires' Bares Notables—once a classic almacén with drinks counter, now a café-bar with porteño memorabilia. The photo matches the cream corner: large oval "BAR EL FEDERAL" sign with bearded figure, scalloped green-and-white awnings over arched doors, iron balcony with green shutters, street plates "Carlos Calvo" and "Peru," and the bright red pillar mailbox on the sidewalk. City tourism highlights old ads, 1920s–30s photos, and a low bar for picadas, tortillas and house sandwiches.
facts.best_time: Late morning or weekday afternoon for a calmer corner photo and café table; Friday–Saturday nights run late. San Telmo weekend fair crowds nearby—arrive early if you want outdoor seats.
facts.how_to_get_there: Carlos Calvo 599 (esquina Perú), San Telmo, Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires. Metro Independencia (Line C/E) or San Juan (Line C) then walk; many colectivos along Defensa / Perú / Independencia.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (Buenos Aires tourism listing and Bares Notables pages active; typical hours roughly Sun–Thu from morning until late night, Fri–Sat later—confirm +54 11 4361-7328). Official notable-bar landmark—not a generic San Telmo café.

image.proof_notes: Commons file shows U Pinkasů facade with U PINKASŮ / již od roku 1843 lettering on Jungmannovo náměstí, Prague (≠ U Fleků / U Zlatého Tygra / U Medvídků).

facts.one_liner: Prague Jungmannovo náměstí beerhall—U PINKASŮ / již od roku 1843 over stone arch.
facts.why_go: U Pinkasů on Jungmannovo náměstí was founded by tailor Jakub Pinkas in 1843 and claims to be the first Prague house to tap bottom-fermented Pilsner Urquell—still pouring tank Prazdroj under Gothic vaults more than 180 years later. The photo matches the cream façade: black "U PINKASŮ" and cursive "již od roku 1843," rustic stone arch entrance, house number 755, planter boxes, and a saint niche (St Lawrence) between upper windows. Prague City Tourism lists Czech classics across rooms and a Gothic garden by Our Lady of the Snows—distinct from U Fleků, U Zlatého Tygra or U Medvídků.
facts.best_time: Weekday mid-morning or early lunch for easier seating in Dolní sněmovna; evenings and weekends fill with locals and visitors. Summer Gothic garden (May–Oct) is walk-in only—arrive early.
facts.how_to_get_there: Jungmannovo náměstí 15/16, 110 00 Praha 1 (Nové Město), steps from the bottom of Wenceslas Square. Metro Můstek (A/B) or Národní třída (B); trams along Vodíčkova / Národní.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official upinkasu.cz and prague.eu: daily 10:00–22:30; Silvester ticketed evenings differ). First Pilsner tap claim is house tradition—not U Fleků / U Zlatého Tygra / U Medvídků. Reserve for peak dinner.

facts.one_liner: Brussels Bourse Belle Époque brasserie—LE CIRIO 1886 neon, Maison Cirio façade, terrace.
facts.why_go: Le Cirio (Maison Cirio / Taverne Cirio) at Rue de la Bourse 18 has been a Brussels brasserie since 1886, steps from the Bourse and Grand-Place, known for Art Nouveau / Belle Époque fittings and the classic half-en-half. The photo matches the ornate dark-wood front: green neon "LE CIRIO," gold "LE CIRIO 1886" on the terrace partition, "MAISON CIRIO" / "TAVERNE CIRIO" lettering, glass awning and packed sidewalk tables. Official site welcomes guests seven days a week for Belgian brasserie plates such as carbonnade—distinct from Delirium, Het Elfde Gebod or In Den Engel.
facts.best_time: Weekday mid-morning or mid-afternoon for a quieter terrace and façade photo; evenings near the Bourse stay busy. Open daily from 10:00—confirm holiday exceptions by phone.
facts.how_to_get_there: Rue de la Bourse 18, 1000 Brussels, opposite/near the former Bourse building. Metro Bourse / De Brouckère; many trams along Boulevard Anspach; short walk from Grand-Place.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official lecirio.be: daily roughly 10:00–00:00; +32 2 512 13 95). Historic Bourse-district brasserie—not Delirium Café, Het Elfde Gebod, or Leuven's In Den Engel. Terrace weather-dependent.
